about.title: Mendota Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Mendota's economy leans heavily on agriculture, packing, and the trucking that moves goods along Rt-33 and Rt-180, and that kind of work carries real physical risk. A fall from a loading dock, a hand caught in machinery, or a strain from repetitive lifting can knock a worker out of a paycheck fast. California generally routes these injuries through workers' compensation, which pays regardless of fault but limits what you can recover. What often gets missed is whether someone outside the employer — a contractor, an equipment manufacturer, a property owner, or another driver — also bears responsibility. That's where a separate injury claim can come into play, alongside the comp claim, not instead of it. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result; we simply connect injured Mendota workers with an independent attorney who can look at both angles and explain, in plain terms, what options may exist for your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Mendota Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Look Beyond the Comp Claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver — may still be liable. An attorney can evaluate whether a separate claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your comp claim. We help connect you quickly so deadlines don't slip by.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on your rights if you feel pressured after speaking up.

items.question: I was hurt while driving for work near Rt-33 in Mendota — do I file workers' comp or a separate claim?
items.answer: Likely both could apply. Workers' comp usually covers your medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but if another driver caused the crash, that's a separate third-party claim with its own 2-year deadline. An independent attorney can help you sort out which applies and how they interact.

items.question: My employer says I waited too long to report my injury — is my claim over?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but timing matters. California generally expects injuries reported to your employer within 30 days, so missing that window can create obstacles worth addressing early with an attorney. Every case has different facts, so it's worth having someone independent review yours.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workplace injury claim?
items.answer: No — retaliation for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can advise you on next steps. LawProactive can connect you with one at no cost to start that conversation.
